summary: Aeromotor LS40K tower on Route 1 in Palm Coast, Flagler County; construction date not found; Weebly listing conflicts on height and name.

facts.design: 100-foot Aeromotor LS40K fire tower with side entry and catwalk (register); a Weebly listing gives 80 feet

events.note: Fire spotting duties discontinued (Weebly Flagler listing)
Registered May 27, 2016; nominated by Bob Spear

evidence.supports: 100-foot Aeromotor LS40K with side entry and catwalk

evidence.quote: It is named after the Wadsworth family, who were prominent in the area, but is sometimes also referred to as Flagler (after the county) or Bunnell (after the nearby town).

corrections.why: The register entry for this tower says 100 feet. The 80-foot figure appears only in the Weebly Flagler listing, which also carries the Southside rename that belongs to the Jacksonville tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 100 feet; Weebly Flagler listing says 80 feet. Used the register figure because it is the tower-specific entry.

notes_for_editor: Construction date, access and agency are not established. The register has no visit reports. The Weebly Flagler listing may describe the Jacksonville tower under this record (see us-fl-southside-forestry); its 80-foot height and 1959 rename are not used as facts. The Florida chapter report says the Jacksonville and Palm Coast towers were both once called Flagler Tower. A News-Journal 2012 article on the Wadsworth tower returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Brief's elevation (13.4 m) and coordinates match the register (44 ft; 29.534523, -81.262412).
